## Declarations and implementations

```plato
//==
// # Images
//
// Sections, in order:
//  - Images
//  - IImage containers

//==
// # Images
//
// Raster data: rectangular grids of pixels. The `IImage` interface
// (`images.concepts.plato`) exposes only dimensions; pixel access lives on the
// concrete types below because pixel representations differ (bytes, floats,
// indices, bits). Unless a type says otherwise, pixel storage is row-major
// starting at the top-left pixel, and a pixel array's Count equals Width times
// Height. Encoded, tiled, animated, and volumetric containers follow in the
// next section.
// Convention: see CONVENTIONS.md - UV origin (origin top-left, V increases
// downward; ImageOrigin.BottomLeft is the opt-in OpenGL order).

// Where pixel row zero sits in an image's coordinate convention: scanline
// order as in most codecs (TopLeft), or OpenGL texture order (BottomLeft).
type ImageOrigin = TopLeft | BottomLeft;

// The in-memory layout of one pixel: channel set, bit depth, and encoding.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Color_depth)
type PixelFormat
    = R8 | RG8 | RGB8 | RGBA8 | BGRA8 | SRGB8 | SRGBA8
    | R16 | RG16 | RGBA16
    | R16F | RG16F | RGBA16F
    | R32F | RG32F | RGB32F | RGBA32F
    | R10G10B10A2 | R11G11B10F
    | Depth16 | Depth24Stencil8 | Depth32F
    | BC1 | BC3 | BC5 | BC7;

//==
// ## Concrete image types

// An 8-bit-per-channel RGBA image, sRGB-encoded: the workhorse storage and
// interop form for display-referred content.
type Bitmap
    implements IImage
{
    Size: IntegerSize2D;
    Pixels: Array<Color8>;
}

// A linear-light RGBA image with unbounded (HDR) range: the working form for
// compositing, filtering, and rendering output.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_dynamic_range)
type FloatImage
    implements IImage
{
    Size: IntegerSize2D;
    Pixels: Array<Color>;
}

// A single-channel image of unbounded scalars: luminance, heights, weights,
// or soft (fractional) masks. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grayscale)
type GrayscaleImage
    implements IImage
{
    Size: IntegerSize2D;
    Values: Array<Number>;
}

// A one-bit-per-pixel image: hard masks, stencils, and region selections.
// True marks a set (selected) pixel.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Binary_image)
type BinaryImage
    implements IImage
{
    Size: IntegerSize2D;
    Values: Array<Boolean>;
}

// A zero-based index of an entry within a palette's color array. -1 marks
// a transparent (unmapped) pixel.
type PaletteIndex
    implements IValue, IHashable, IComparable, IIndex
{
    Value: Integer;
}

// A palette-indexed image: each pixel stores a zero-based index into Palette.
// An index of -1 marks a transparent (unmapped) pixel.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indexed_color)
type IndexedImage
    implements IImage
{
    Size: IntegerSize2D;
    Indices: Array<PaletteIndex>;
    Palette: Palette;
}

// A per-pixel scene-depth image. Depths are normalized to [0, 1] between the
// Near and Far distances that produced them.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Depth_map)
type DepthImage
    implements IImage
{
    Size: IntegerSize2D;
    Depths: Array<Number>;
    Near: Number;
    Far: Number;
}

// An image of unit direction vectors (a tangent-space or world-space normal
// map), stored unencoded: components in [-1, 1], not remapped to color range.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Normal_mapping)
type NormalImage
    implements IImage
{
    Size: IntegerSize2D;
    Normals: Array<Vector3D>;
}

//==
// # IImage containers
//
// Images that hold something other than one plain 2D pixel grid: compressed
// file payloads, mip pyramids, tile grids, frame sequences, regions of
// interest, voxel volumes, and cubemap face sets. The single-grid pixel types
// they are built from are the section above.

//==
// ## Encoded, tiled, and multi-resolution images

// A compressed image file format; Hdr is Radiance HDR.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Image_file_format)
type ImageCodec
    = Png | Jpeg | WebP | Gif | Bmp | Tga | Tiff | Exr | Hdr | Ktx2 | Dds | Avif | Heic;

// An image in compressed (file) form: an opaque byte payload plus the codec
// that produced it. Each element of Bytes is one octet in [0, 255].
type EncodedImage
    implements IValue
{
    Codec: ImageCodec;
    Bytes: Array<Integer>;
}

// A full mipmap pyramid. Levels[0] is the base image; each subsequent level
// halves both dimensions (rounding down, minimum 1) until 1x1.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mipmap)
type MipChain
    implements IValue
{
    Levels: Array<FloatImage>;
}
```
